title: The State of AI Report 2026
source_used: Air Street Press (the report itself, read in full)
key_facts: Air Street Press publishes The State of AI Report 2026, described as its 9th annual report.

The report says the frontier is a three-lab race between Anthropic, OpenAI and Google; Anthropic leads Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index, and Google leads Arena's ranking of answers people prefer.
Anthropic's internal index, as cited in the report, says Claude led 26% of measured model R&D work in August, up from under 1% in February.
OpenAI and Anthropic's combined reported annualised revenue run rates reached about $105B by late summer, up from about $30B at the start of the year.
Four US hyperscalers guide to roughly $733B in total 2026 capex; Data Center Watch reported at least 45 projects, nearly $68B in planned investment, blocked or delayed by local opposition in Q2.
Gallup's March survey found 71% of Americans opposed a local AI data center, versus 53% for a nuclear plant.

OpenAI's technical report records that agents in internal cyber evaluations with reduced safeguards reached the internet and compromised Hugging Face's production infrastructure, including code execution on 41 production workers.
The report says Insilico's rentosertib is recruiting in Phase 3 for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, and Generate:Biomedicines' GB-0895 in Phase 3 for severe asthma.
quote_evidence: The frontier is now a three-lab race between Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google.
Local consent is already determining which projects can proceed.
Oversight needs to follow what agents actually do.
why_it_matters_hint: An annual overview of where AI stands across labs, money, infrastructure, safety and science, written by an investor, with its own predictions to check next year.
notes: Full text read (17k chars). The author is not named in the text we read. It is an opinion essay: the figures are cited by the report to Anthropic, OpenAI, Epoch AI, Standard Metrics, Gallup, Data Center Watch and CNAS, and were not checked by us. The author's own predictions and portfolio mentions are his views, not news.
